Subject: Suitable reception and entertainment of Prince Henry of Prussia, while sojourning in the United States, ordered.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 188; X Richardson 521. TR Presidential Library record uo-018, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = EO 162** (Jan. 24, 1902). NARA's *Preliminary Inventory of the General Records of the Department of State* (PI 157, 1963), entry 183, lists the "Executive order of January 24, 1902, appointing delegates to make arrangements for Prince Henry's reception and entertainment"; Lord's Feb. 5 date is a second dating of the same document. See research entry #114.

Subject: Appointment of a clerk, War Department, at $1,000 per annum for duty at the White House, without examination, authorized.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 191; (1903 CSR 72). TR Presidential Library record uo-042, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 185** (July 30, 1902), "Amending Civil Service Rules to Except War Department Clerk in White House Duty from Examination." Same date, same subject. Lord's only citation is a parenthesized back-reference.

Subject: Certain described lands in Puerto Rico reserved for naval purposes.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 194; (EO 220). TR Presidential Library record uo-061, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= Proclamation 502** (June 26, 1903), *Reservation of Lands in Puerto Rico for Naval Purposes* (33 Stat. 2314; research entry #44). Same date, same subject. Lord's only citation, "(EO 220)", is an order whose own title calls this document the "Proclamation of June 26, 1903."

Subject: Ten specified persons appointed to the Commerce and Labor Department, without examination.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 195; X Richardson 632; 1904 CSR 82. TR Presidential Library record uo-064, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 223** (July 13, 1903), "Authorizing Appointment of Ten Persons to Positions in Department of Commerce and Labor Without Examination." Same date, same subject.

Subject: Notaries public in government employ forbidden to accept compensation for notarial acts of interest to the government.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 201; (1906 CSA 25; 1908 CSA 27; EO of Mar. 31, 1905). TR Presidential Library record uo-101, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = EO 288½.** Commerce Department Circulars Nos. 55 (Jan. 1905) and 68 (Apr. 7, 1905) and the Jan. 4, 1905 press (*Atlanta Constitution*, "No Graft for Notaries") carry the single order; Lord's 1944 numbered volume lists it as 288½. See entry #114.

Subject: Oregon City, Oreg., Land Office abolished (eff. June 30, 1905); business/records to the Portland office.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 201; (1905 GLO 185). TR Presidential Library record uo-105, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 310-B** (Mar. 21, 1905), "Land Office at Oregon City Transferred to Portland." Same date, same subject.

Subject: Ironton, Mo., Land Office abolished (eff. June 30, 1905); to the Springfield office.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 201; (1905 GLO 172). TR Presidential Library record uo-107, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = EO 321-A.** As for no. 106 (GLO FY1905; *Oakland Tribune*, May 13, 1905). See entry #114.

Subject: Vernal, Utah, designated the Land Office for the Uintah Land District (act of Mar. 3, 1905, 33 Stat. L. 1014).
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 202; (1905 GLO 190). TR Presidential Library record uo-108, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 321-E** (May 1, 1905), "Establishment of Uintah Land District." Same date, same subject. Lord's own numbered-series volume carries the May 1, 1905 date (research entry #114).

Subject: Akron, Colo., Land Office abolished (eff. June 30, 1905); to the Sterling office.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 201; (1905 GLO 158). TR Presidential Library record uo-106, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = EO 321-F.** Lord's 1944 numbered volume and the GLO FY1905 report treat the Akron abolition as the one numbered order; Lord's bracketed "Mar. 21" was his inference. See entry #114.

Subject: Certain lands near Central, Alaska, reserved for military purposes.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 202; (1916 MR 478). TR Presidential Library record uo-109, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = part of EO 328-B.** Wickersham, *Bibliography of Alaskan Literature* (1927), lists the May 24, 1905 order covering the telegraph right-of-way and stations including Central and Summit, and EO 702 (Oct. 23, 1907) releasing "reservations at Central and Summit made by Executive Order of May 24, 1905." Nos. 109 and 110 are one numbered order. See entry #114.

Subject: Certain lands at Summit, Alaska, reserved for military purposes.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 202; (1916 MR 489). TR Presidential Library record uo-110, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = part of EO 328-B.** See no. 109.

Subject: Wichita Forest Reserve, Oklahoma, redesignated as a game preserve.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 202; EO 1147; 1910 MR 301; 1916 MR 310. TR Presidential Library record uo-111, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= Proclamation 563** (June 2, 1905), *Redesignating the Wichita Forest Reserve, Oklahoma, as a Game Preserve* (34 Stat. 3062). It is not an executive order. Lord's "Fort Sill (water-supply)" wording comes from Taft's EO 1147 of Dec. 15, 1909 (research entry #114).

Subject: Grass Island Military Reservation, Wash., established.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 202; (1916 MR 481). TR Presidential Library record uo-112, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 330-A** (June 12, 1905), "Approval of War Secretary Recommendation to Reserve Grass Island, Gray's Harbor, Washington, for Military Purposes." Same date, same subject. It was abolished by EO 432 (Mar. 28, 1906).

Subject: Santa Clara Pueblo Indian Reservation, New Mexico Territory, enlarged, subject to valid existing rights.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 202; III Kappler 687; I IR 127; (1905 CIA 496). TR Presidential Library record uo-113, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 344-B** (July 29, 1905), "Reserving Certain Described Lands for the Pueblo Indians of New Mexico Belonging to the Pueblo of Santa Clara." Same date, same subject.

Subject: All Navy vessels to be officially designated by name preceded by "United States Ship" or "U.S.S." and no other words/letters.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 203; (1907 Doc. Cat. 1384). TR Presidential Library record uo-116, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 549** (Jan. 8, 1907). Same date, same operative text (research entries #91, #110).

Subject: Civil Service General Rule II and Rule X amended to permit transfer of a meritorious overseas non-classified employee into a competitive classified position, with CSC approval.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 203; 1907 CSR 127; (1908 CSA 38, 59). TR Presidential Library record uo-120, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **Confirmed 2026-10-12 = part of EO 679.** The Civil Service Commission's *Twenty-fourth Report* (1907), p. 127, prints the single Aug. 12, 1907 order: the A. J. Robinson classification followed by the general clause for similar overseas cases that Lord lists separately. See entry #114.

Subject: Certain lands at Rapids, on the Yukon River, Alaska, reserved for military purposes.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 204; (1916 MR 486). TR Presidential Library record uo-122, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 792** (May 4, 1908), "Reserving Fourteen Tracts of Land in Alaska for Stations on Third Section of United States Military Telegraph Lines" (research entry #114).

Subject: Biliran Island Military Reservation, Leyte Province, P. I., established.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 204; (1916 MR 477). TR Presidential Library record uo-123, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 796** (May 13, 1908), "Reserving Certain Lands on Island of Biliran, Philippine Islands, for Military Purposes." Same date, same subject.

Subject: Deschutes National Forest, Oreg., established and boundaries defined.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 204; (EO 912). TR Presidential Library record uo-124, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 816** (approved June 13, 1908, effective July 1). Lord entered the effective date. EO 912 (July 14, 1908) is a later boundary redefinition (research entry #114).

Subject: Fremont National Forest, Oreg., reorganized and boundaries defined.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 204; (EO 913). TR Presidential Library record uo-125, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 817** (approved June 13, 1908, effective July 1). The Fremont itself dates from Proc. 651 of Sept. 17, 1906. EO 913 (July 14, 1908) is a later boundary redefinition (research entry #114).

Subject: Round Top and Sugar Loaf Military Reservation, Honolulu, Oahu, Hawaii, established.
Citation: Clifford L. Lord (ed.), List and Index of Presidential Executive Orders: Unnumbered Series (Newark: Historical Records Survey, WPA, 1943), printed p. 204; (1910 MR 92; 1916 MR 104). TR Presidential Library record uo-126, accessed 2026-11-12.
Reason: **= EO 978** (Nov. 24, 1908), "Reserving Lands on Oahu … for Observation Stations in Connection with Defensive Works." Lord's Dec. 1 date is a compiler's slip from War Dept. G.O. 200, which also published EO 985 of Dec. 1 (research entry #114).
